items.prompt:
[S2] A triangle has sides 9 cm, 12 cm and 15 cm.
Show that it is right-angled.
items.solution:
9² + 12² = 81 + 144 = 225 = 15².
Since the square on the longest side equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides, the triangle is right-angled (converse of Pythagoras’ theorem).
acceptedAnswers: right-angled at the vertex between 9 cm and 12 cm
items.stem: A triangle has sides 9 cm, 12 cm and 15 cm.

items.solution:
Area ratio △ADE : △ABC = (2/5)² = 4 : 25.
Area of △ABC = 12 × 25/4 = 75 cm².
Area of DBCE = 75 − 12 = 63 cm².

items.prompt:
[S2] A merchant mixes 20 kg of tea costing $80 per kg with x kg of tea costing $120 per kg. The mixture is sold at $95 per kg, which is exactly the cost price of the mixture.
(a) Write down an equation in x.
items.solution:
Total cost = 20 × 80 + 120x = 1600 + 120x.
Total mass = 20 + x, so the cost per kg is (1600 + 120x)/(20 + x) = 95.
items.stem: A merchant mixes 20 kg of tea costing $80 per kg with x kg of tea costing $120 per kg. The mixture is sold at $95 per kg, which is exactly the cost price of the mixture.

items.prompt:
[S2] Class X has mean ≈ 65.58 and range 40; Class Y has mean ≈ 65.75 and range 12. Class X’s top score is 85 and its lowest is 45.
(d) Two parents argue: “Class Y must be better — its mean is higher.” “No, Class X must be better — its top student scored 85.” Evaluate both claims using your results.
items.solution:
The first claim is weak: the two means differ by only about 0.2 marks, which is negligible — not evidence that Class Y is better.
The second claim is also weak: one top score of 85 does not describe the class; indeed Class X also has a very low score of 45, giving it the larger range. Class X is more spread out (some very strong and some weak students), while Class Y is uniformly around 65.
